sections.heading: Comments in C
sections.body: Comments are notes for humans. They help explain code and make it easier to read. They can also be used to temporarily "disable" code while testing. Comments can be single-line or multi-line. Remember: Comments are ignored by the compiler, so they do not affect your program's output.

sections.heading: Single-line Comments
sections.body: Single-line comments start with two forward slashes (//). Any text between // and the end of the line is ignored by the compiler. This example uses a single-line comment before a line of code:

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: This example uses a single-line comment at the end of a line of code:
sections.code:
// This is a comment
printf("Hello World!");

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: You can also use // to disable a single line of code:
sections.code: printf("Hello World!"); // This is a comment

sections.heading: Example
sections.code:
printf("This will run");
// printf("This will NOT run");

sections.heading: Multi-line Comments
sections.body: Multi-line comments start with /* and end with */. Any text between /* and */ will be ignored by the compiler:

sections.heading: Example
sections.body: It is up to you which you want to use. Normally, we use // for short comments and /* */ for longer comments. Good to know: Before C99 (released in 1999), you could only use multi-line comments in C.
